comparison.objective: Candidate commissions a shock absorber by tuning and locking damping, then validating repeated carriage stops; pr-277 installs two protective-grounding clamps in a safety-critical order.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate requires recessed hex-key engagement, collar fine-rotation, counterholding, torque-limited locking, and response-based retuning. pr-277 requires transporting cable-linked clamps, seating jaws on bars, and turning long eye-screw handles to achieve clamp force.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires two acceptable physical impact cycles within energy, velocity, and 12 mm stroke limits, with no bottoming or setting drift. pr-277 requires ground-first attachment, both clamps at ≥120 N, forbidden-bar avoidance, release, and a 40 N tug test. Candidate rubric lacks numeric definitions for excessive rebound, overload, collar drift tolerance, and locking torque/thread damage.
comparison.reason: Turning and tightening are shared generic primitives, but the tested abilities—dynamic damper tuning and retained setting versus ordered installation of a flexible grounding set—are meaningfully different.
